To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the titrations of the two dyes with three polymers have been used to estimate accurately the equivalent weights of all the polymers.

(1) The titrations of DMMB by TA, DNA and chondroitin sulfate A can be used for the accurate estimation of the equivalent weights of these biopolymers; (2) The titrational curves of DMMB and AO by TA are sigmoidal and can be used to obtain the equivalent weight of TA; (3) The titrative curve of AO by TA is sigmoidal, but that of DMMB is not; (4)

the titrations of DMMB by chondroitin sulfate A (CSA) and teichoic acids (TAs), and of AO by DNA and TAs, are simple, accurate and reproducible methods for the quantitative estimation and equivalent weight determination of anionic polymeric substances.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new and more sensitive methods for the quantitative estimation and characterization of the anionic polymers.
the development of a simple and accurate method to determine the equivalent weight of teichoic acids.
the development of new analytical procedures for the determination of biopolymers and other macromolecules, and for the estimation of their molecular weight.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the titration method described here is the most accurate method of determining the equivalent weight of TA, and that the method described is the most accurate for determining the equivalent weight and the concentration of TA.

the method is applicable to the estimation of anionic biopolysars of known and unknown equivalent weights, and that the method can be used for the quantitative estimation, and the estimation of the equivalent weights, of the polymers.
the spectrophotometric and fluorescence titration methods described here are simple, accurate and rapid methods of estimating the equivalent weights of biopolymers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the titration of anionic biopolysers by DMMB or AO can be carried out in the presence of 10% (w/v) ethanol, in 0.05 M NaCl solution, at pH 5.0, and that the titrations can yield equivalent weights of the biopolymers.
these methods can be used as a rapid and convenient alternative to the conventional methods of titration of anionic polymeric materials.
the titrations of the two dyes, DMMB and AO, by TA can be used for the estimation of the latter in the range 0.2-2.0 mg/ml.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DMMB can be used as a sensitive probe to detect TA in the presence of chondroitin sulfate and DNA.
DMMB and AO can be used for spectrophotometic and spectrofluorimetric titrations of TA.
the dye binding efficiencies of the three polymers, as estimated by the two dyes, differ significantly.
